description_en: The Bābiro Maṣṭā temple, located in the village of Bābiro on the northern bank of the Tilā Nadī river, is an important religious site dedicated to the god Bābiro Maṣṭā. It is one of three temples dedicated to the god Bābiro Maṣṭā. One temple, theghar thān, is located in the village. It was under renovation during the Spring of 2022. The other one, thebān thān, or forest temple, stands on the hill overlooking the village. A flight of 475 steps climbs from Bābiro Māru to the Bābiro Bān thān. Māru is the term given to oracular temples located in the outskirts of settlements (Campbell 1978).The Bābiro Maṣṭā temple follows a rectangular floor plan with an east-west orientation. Entry to the temple is through the southern side, leading to the central room where the medium's throne (gaddi,gādi) is located. The throne comprises a square cemented platform upon which the medium (dhāmī) sits while possessed, reciting the story of the possessing divinity (paṛheli) (Campbell 1978,see alsoShrestha-Schipper 2003andYasuno 2018).Within the western wall of the throne's platform, an important feature is a stone stele. This stele portrays a standing male figure holding a staff in its left arm. The figure is believed to represent the deity Bābiro Maṣṭā and is distinctively depicted with its penis hanging between the legs. This stele serves as a significant symbol within the temple.Adjacent to the main room, towards the west, there is a storage room. This room provides space for storing various items related to the temple's rituals and offerings. To the east of the entrance, there is a designated area enclosed by a colonnade. This space contains a central fireplace known askuṇḍaoragenā, which is embedded into the floor. The fireplace likely holds ceremonial significance within the temple complex.Inside and outside the Bābiro Maṣṭā temple, devotees have donated wooden anthropomorphic sculptures and carved poles, primarily situated on the eastern wall and in the northeast corner. These sacred artifacts serve as significant religious symbols within the temple complex.The exact age of the temple remains unknown, as there is no specific information available regarding its antiquity.
